# First native Full Delivery provider preparation

Owner: parent. This is a reviewable mutation specification for the existing Write Backlog GitHub adapter; it is not a provider executor. Native comparison stays on hold until all exact readbacks below exist. Authorization is restricted to the isolated private fixture project/repository, run-owned backlog objects/branches and draft PR/report retention. Preserve all prior run histories. No merge, release or canonical-source publication.

## Fixed product and authority

Repository: stefan-garofalo/v43-admission-fixture-20260906-01a0777c, private. Fixed main commit A contains the starter browser product. The child commit B on fixture-seed/full-small adds accepted SPEC/PLAN and workflow guidance. This meaningful spec difference permits early draft PRs against main. Keep both refs fixed for all small fixtures; other families receive their own fixed base/seed refs.

After pushing A/B, read back repository node ID, visibility, refs/commits/trees, B ancestry and exact docs/specs/full-small/SPEC.md blob bytes. The immutable blob URL uses B, never a branch name. SPEC has OUT-001, AC-1–AC-5, accepted technical/testing decisions and verification seams. A local URL or push acknowledgement is not retention proof.

## Shared private Projects V2 operating surface

Create or reuse only the exact isolated project identity. Resolve and retain its node ID, private visibility, owner and linked repository. Product brief: safe browser slug preview. Target user: a user preparing a URL slug. Product boundary: local browser form; no persistence/auth/deployment. Wiki authority: retained fixture SPEC/README. Operating rule: preserve each measured run's isolated issue/history; no release/merge.

Required configured fields and stable options:

| Field | Options and meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Product Area | Admission fixture (one durable product-area identity) |
| Initiative | Browser slug preview (one durable initiative identity scoped to that area) |
| Kind | Epic, Story, Task, Fog, Grilling, Research, Prototype |

Record durable identity mapping in Project README when option descriptions cannot carry it. Read back existing Status options; choose the same initial not-started state for every run. Preserve any exact status IDs needed for observed work start/completion.

Required semantically equivalent views: Product Map (hierarchy and semantic fields), Roadmap (milestone plus Story/Task progress), Fogs (Kind Fog), Current Delivery (Story/Task work and native blocker visibility). Use native supported createProjectV2View/updateProjectV2View fields: name, layout, configuration.visibleFieldIds, filter. Retain exact view configurations; if a required representation cannot be expressed or read back, report that exact capability boundary instead of substituting a flat Issues surface.

## Per-run validated mutation topology

Use delivery projection mode against verified immutable SPEC B. One Epic describes the browser capability; one Story is OUT-001; one vertical Task implements AC-1–AC-5. The pure helper and sole form consumer stay one owner-ready Task. The small Task graph has no blocker edges; later skewed/medium fixtures exercise nonempty native relations. Before provider writes, validate the complete graph through the existing provider-neutral validator.

Each run has its own Epic, Story, Task and V* milestone with an explicit run identity. Same provider topology, acceptance text, source authority, fields, initial status and milestone semantics apply to both variants; only stable IDs/URLs/run suffixes differ. Never reset or reuse prior run mutation histories.

Parent-first mutation envelope:

1. Resolve isolated project/fields/views and create the run milestone with product goal and included OUT-001.
2. Create enriched Epic in the Project. Its body retains immutable SPEC URL, OUT-001, accepted AC text, technical/testing decisions, verification seams, fixture/run provenance and wiki identity. Read it back before dependent creation.
3. Create Story as native Epic sub-issue with same authority enrichment and run V* milestone. Set exact Product Area, Initiative and Kind=Story options. Read back parent, membership, fields and milestone.
4. Create Task as native Story sub-issue with same milestone and exact authority/acceptance. Set Kind=Task and the same semantic fields. Read back full parent chain, Project membership, milestone, source links, node ID and URL. Read native blockers as the empty set, not an omitted field.
5. Retain the Write Backlog result plus raw readback identities/hashes. Fog provenance is explicitly not applicable because no Finder/Fog intake exists. Do not invent one.

## Hydration and launch readiness

Per run, clone exact B into its authorized run branch. Set .devpunks/settings.json backlogProjectUrl to the exact verified Project URL. Replace PLAN TASK_ID/TASK_URL placeholders with that run's native Task identity/URL and retain its parent Story/milestone/Project/field/graph readback in CONTEXT.json. Commit/push only this identity hydration on the run branch, preserving the product and SPEC bytes. The source selected workflow then searches for/creates the actual matching draft PR and records exact readback before applicable dispatch. Selected reusable skill copies remain ignored and unpushed; authored project references and retained evidence can be committed.

CONTEXT.json must contain exact run ID, repository/project node IDs and URLs, allowed branch/base refs, seed commit/tree, immutable spec commit/path/blob/SHA256/URL plus readback provenance, current Backlog Result path/hash, Task alias mapping, Epic/Story/Task/milestone IDs/URLs, semantic option IDs, native parent/blocker facts, initial state and exact readback provenance. Preserve this file as task evidence, while keeping it ignored from product commits.

Readiness requires no placeholders in PLAN or settings, current routed product meaning under apps/wiki/content/docs/project/README.md, exact seed/source/config/runtime identities, current remote spec/backlog proof, correct branch/base, identical initial product bytes and normalized plan behavior, and native provider/browser capacity. Compare provider identity mappings explicitly; never report unequal raw provider IDs as identical artifacts. Retain changed metadata paths separately from the identical initial product/source authority. Any missing field or mismatched readback keeps native execution on hold.
